A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same S3T research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original vision, language-understanding, instruction-tuning, deletion-performance, and ablation experiments in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds deletion-time measurements and evaluations of cyclic rotation and prior-aware sequence selection.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 replaces uniform-prior BMS selection with iterative cyclic rotation. For nonuniform priors and B <= L, conditional sampling gives way to score-weighted BMS using Hungarian matching and highest-score sequence selection; conditional sampling remains for larger budgets. The underlying sequential LoRA training remains unchanged.

E1.justification: The vision, GLUE/SuperGLUE, instruction-tuning, and LLM evaluation datasets remain unchanged. v2 adds evaluated sequence-selection scenarios with nonuniform, Dirichlet-sampled deletion priors in Section 4.3 and Appendix C.3; v1 discusses known priors but does not report these experiments.

E2.justification: Figure 6 adds ProtoSISA and full retraining alongside SISA. The new nonuniform-prior panels in Figure 8 compare BMS with Conditional Sampling, as identified by their legends, although nearby prose calls it random sampling. Appendix Figure 15 adds Sorted Cyclic Rotation. These substantially expand the deletion and sequence-selection comparisons.

E3.justification: Sequence evaluation changes from average minimum edit distance to reported average edit distance and adds deletion-prior scores, an L=5 budget sweep through 120, and nonuniform-prior tests. A new CIFAR-10 protocol measures cumulative checkpoint-switching and retraining time over 1,000 deletion requests. The existing fine-tuning hyperparameters in Table 2 are unchanged.

E4.justification: The single BMS diversity comparison expands into cyclic-rotation budget sensitivity and prior-aware sequence-quality analyses. Appendix C.3 additionally compares BMS with sorted cyclic rotation, examining score differences despite equal diversity. Existing slice-deletion, layer-allocation, sequential-training, training-time, and storage analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly reports averaging over ten Dirichlet-sampled deletion priors for the new sequence-selection analyses. v1 provides no corresponding repetition count. Existing parenthetical uncertainty values in Table 1 and uncertainty displays in retained plots remain unchanged; no increase in repetitions for those experiments is established.

E6.justification: The LLM scores in Table 1 and storage/deletion-rate values in Table 3 are unchanged. v2 adds comparator curves, cyclic-rotation and prior-aware selection findings, and deletion-time results. Figure 9 newly reports cumulative deletion time lower by factors of 2.8 versus SISA and 25 versus full retraining after 1,000 requests.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 generalizes the deletion-rate bound from B >= L to O(mL log(m min(B,L))). The retention proof replaces B'(1-k/L)^r with 1-[1-(1-k/L)^r]^B', changes the budget cap from binomial(L,k) to L!/(L-k)!, and introduces explicit random-sequence and uniform-prior assumptions. v2 also defines a prior-dependent sequence score; the existing BMS diversity lemma is relocated and adapted.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central claims of efficient exact unlearning, parameter isolation, and improved deletion capability. The introduction replaces its specific claim of an optimal graph-matching selection algorithm with a contribution comprising several sequence-selection approaches, modestly revising the contribution framing.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes random-sequence retention theory from practical cyclic selection and leaves cyclic optimality and joint BMS diversity/score optimality open. It removes v1's dedicated limitation concerning expensive high-budget, large-model offline training, although the general offline-training tradeoff remains elsewhere. Interpretations of retained benchmark and ablation results largely persist.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds cyclic-selection pseudocode and weighted-matching implementation details, and corrects model reinsertion in deletion pseudocode from set difference to union. It acknowledges unspecified corner-case selection heuristics. Hardware, optimizer, training precision, and Table 2 hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds related work including Park, Zhang, Lucki, and Xu (2024), plus Kuhn and Tomizawa for weighted matching, while removing the Cormen, Gibbons, and Hopcroft-Karp references. The overall positioning around SISA and the approximate/exact unlearning distinction remains stable.

P1.justification: The main section order and much of the prose are retained. v2 edits the introduction and background, integrates the roadmap into the introduction, adds a worked workflow example, moves design choices to Appendix C.2, and reorders appendix proofs. These are localized editorial and structural changes alongside the substantive additions.

P2.justification: Figures 3 and 4 are redrawn for cyclic rotation and weighted matching, and Figure 8 expands from one plot to three panels. New displays cover deletion time, cyclic-selection trees, and sorted-rotation comparisons. The conditional-sampling diagram moves to Appendix Figure 11. The document also adopts new headers, heading styles, table-caption placement, and extensive figure reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical support for practical efficiency through additional deletion comparisons and direct deletion-time measurements, and more clearly qualifies the theory's applicability. These gains are tempered by unspecified cyclic-selection heuristics, the remaining gap between retention theory and practical cyclic selection, and removal of the explicit high-budget training-cost limitation. The evidence supports a positive but limited overall quality improvement.
